newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan rupee ends higher on devaluation denial.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan rupee ends higher on devaluation denial.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee ended 0.03 up to 41.15 to the dollar on Tuesday after Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz denied that the government planned to devalue the rupee, dealers said.

"The rupee bounced back after the finance minister said the government did not plan to devalue the rupee," a dealer said. The rupee had slipped on an earlier statement by Aziz hinting at the possibility of a marginal rupee devaluation.
The State Bank of Pakistan rate, last changed on October 22, was 40.1200/40.3206 to the dollar. The premium on foreign exchange bearer certificates ended stable at 2.60 percent.
